archetypes.name: code-robustness
archetypes.rationale: The duplicate_edges_skipped counter in plan_inherited_main and the _write_outcome last-status-wins pattern both have subtle correctness properties worth independent scrutiny.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the `duplicate_edges_skipped` counter logic in `plan_inherited_main` (python/combine_issues.py, around the `edge_sources[edge]` accumulation loop): the condition `if source in edge_sources[edge] or edge_sources[edge]` increments the counter whenever the dict entry is non-empty, which fires on the first additional source for any edge — verify whether this accurately counts deduplication events or over-counts. Examine `_write_outcome` (python/combine_issues.py): it iterates all write-result rows for a phase and records the last-seen status, so a retry success would only be detected if it appears last in the list; check whether this is consistent with the test in `test_close_eligible_ignores_retried_safe_write_failure`. Also check whether `_parse_prose_blocks` in combine_issues.py silently swallows parsing errors — unlike `blocker.parse_prose_blockers` it has no top-level try/except, meaning a malformed input could propagate an exception through `prose_audit_main` as an unhandled crash. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: dep-resolution
archetypes.rationale: _resolve_repo calls gh.resolve_repo which is not shown as added in the diff — if that symbol does not exist the entire OOS dependency workflow silently breaks at runtime.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that `gh.resolve_repo` (called by `_resolve_repo` in python/combine_issues.py) is already exported from `python/gh.py`. The diff adds only `issue_blocking_read` to gh.py; if `resolve_repo` is absent, every new CLI verb that omits `--repo` would fail with an AttributeError rather than a clean error message. Also check that `close_sources_main` correctly propagates the `--combined-issue` validation error to stderr before any GitHub API calls, and confirm the pre-close `_source_close_skip_reason` guard handles missing or malformed `state` fields in the `gh issue view` JSON response without silently marking sources as skippable. Finally, verify the `--defer-close` output contract — the diff emits `CLOSED_ISSUES=0` unconditionally when defer is set, which callers in SKILL.md are told to stop using for tally purposes, but check whether any surviving code path still reads `CLOSED_ISSUES` from apply output and would misinterpret the zero. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: duplication-review
archetypes.rationale: The negation/fence/example regex constants and _has_scoped_negation helper are defined identically in both blocker.py and combine_issues.py, creating a divergence risk.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect whether `_CODE_FENCE_RE`, `_MARKDOWN_PREFIX_RE`, `_EXAMPLE_PREFIX_RE`, `_NEGATION_RE`, `_NEGATION_SCOPE_BOUNDARY_RE`, and `_has_scoped_negation` in python/combine_issues.py are exact copies of the same symbols in python/blocker.py, and assess whether this duplication is intentional module isolation or an oversight that will diverge silently if one copy is updated. Check whether the old `_repo()` function in combine_issues.py is still called anywhere now that `_resolve_repo()` wraps it — if it is dead code its removal would reduce confusion. Also review whether `_edge_list` (python/combine_issues.py) is used anywhere in the diff or is an unreferenced helper. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
